54	IDCOUNT_RE = re.compile(r'^(.*)_([0-9]+)$')

57	def unique(id: str, ids: MutableSet[str], counters: dict[str, int] | None = None) -> str:
58	    """ Ensure id is unique in set of ids. Append '_1', '_2'... if not
59	
60	    `counters` is an optional cache which maps a base id to the highest `n` for which
61	    `base_1` through `base_n` are all known to be in `ids`. When the same cache is passed
62	    along with the same `ids` on every call, a repeated id skips past the suffixes which
63	    earlier calls already found to be taken rather than checking each of them again.
64	    """
65	    if id in ids or not id:
66	        m = IDCOUNT_RE.match(id)
67	        if m:
68	            base, count = m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
69	        else:
70	            base, count = id, 0
71	        skip = False
72	        if counters is not None:
73	            known = counters.get(base, 0)
74	            # Only skip ahead when this id falls within the run of suffixes known to be
75	            # taken, or is the next one after it, as any later suffix may still be free.
76	            if count <= known or id == f'{base}_{known + 1}':
77	                skip = True
78	                count = max(count, known)
79	        count += 1
80	        while f'{base}_{count}' in ids:
81	            count += 1
82	        id = f'{base}_{count}'
83	        if skip:
84	            # Every suffix from `base_1` through the new id is now known to be taken.
85	            counters[base] = count
86	    ids.add(id)

# Spec: TOC is kind of useless for non-English docs ## 1. Summary and scope **Problem [FACT]:** The issue says that for docs written in Hindi and Russian, "the links are all `#_1`, `#_2`, ... and when we share a link to a section nobody can tell where it goes." **Root cause [FACT, from the code]:** The default `slugify` in `markdown/extensions/toc.py:39-46` runs `unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', ...)` and then `.encode('ascii', 'ignore')` whenever `unicode=False`, which is the default. That removes every Cyrillic and Devanagari character, so the slug is an empty string. `unique()` (`markdown/extensions/toc.py:57-87`) then turns an empty id into `_1`, `_2`, … (`if id in ids or not id:` → base `''` → `'_1'`). The treeprocessor calls the configured slugify at `markdown/extensions/toc.py:404`. **Existing mitigation [FACT]:** A Unicode-preserving function, `markdown.extensions.toc.slugify_unicode` (`toc.py:49-51`), already exists. It is documented only in one sentence (`docs/extensions/toc.md:219-220`) and tested only with Japanese (`tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py:1199-1217`). Users have to opt in to it with `TocExtension(slugify=slugify_unicode)`. **Secondary defect [INFERRED, from Python `re` semantics]:** The Unicode path strips characters with `re.sub(r'[^\w\s-]', '', value)`. In Python, `\w` does not match combining marks (Unicode categories Mn and Mc). Devanagari vowel signs and the virama are combining marks, so even with `slugify_unicode` the heading `नमस्ते दुनिया` becomes `नमसत-दनय`. The Hindi words are mangled, so the anchors are still not readable to Hindi users. **In scope:** - When the default `slugify` is configured, headings whose text has no ASCII-transliterable word characters get a readable Unicode slug instead of `_n` (FR-001). - Unicode slugs keep combining marks, so Devanagari (and other abugida) words stay intact (FR-002). - The `slugify` option documentation in `docs/extensions/toc.md` explains this behaviour (part of FR-001). **Out of scope:** - Changing the default slug for any heading that already produces a non-empty ASCII slug, for example `žlutý kůň` → `zluty-kun`, or `Глава 1` → `1`. See Q-002. - Transliterating non-Latin scripts into Latin (for example `Привет` → `privet`). This would need a new dependency or tables. See Q-001. - Explicit ids set with `attr_list` (`{#id}`), the `unique()` suffix algorithm, and custom user-supplied `slugify` callables. - Percent-encoding of `href` values. ## 2. Functional requirements ```yaml id: "FR-001" title: "Fall back to a Unicode slug when the default slug is empty" statement: "When the toc extension uses the default slugify callable and the ASCII slug for a heading is an empty string, the system SHALL use the Unicode-preserving slug of the same heading text (as produced by slugify_unicode, subject to FR-002) as the heading id and TOC anchor, and SHALL fall back to the existing `_n` behaviour only if that Unicode slug is also empty." epistemic_status: "INFERRED" source: "Issue #5: 'the links are all `#_1`, `#_2`, ... nobody can tell where it goes ... Can toc be improved for this?'; markdown/extensions/toc.py:39-46, 57-87, 404; docs/extensions/toc.md:206-220" actor: "Documentation author writing headings in a non-Latin script; reader following a shared section link" priority: "MUST_HAVE" readiness_status: "PROVISIONAL" dependencies: ["FR-002", "ASSUMP-001", "ASSUMP-002", "Q-001", "Q-002"] inputs: - {name: "heading text", type: "str", description: "Plain text of a Markdown heading"} - {name: "slugify config", type: "callable", description: "TocExtension 'slugify' option; default markdown.extensions.toc.slugify"} - {name: "separator config", type: "str", description: "TocExtension 'separator' option; default '-'"} outputs: - {name: "id attribute", type: "str", description: "id on the heading element and href target in the TOC"} acceptance_criteria: - id: "AC-FR-001-01" scenario: "Cyrillic heading with default configuration" given: "markdown.markdown('# Привет мир', extensions=['toc'])" when: "the document is rendered" then: "output is exactly '

Привет мир

'" - id: "AC-FR-001-02" scenario: "Repeated Cyrillic headings remain unique and readable" given: "source '# Привет\\n\\n# Привет' with extensions=['toc'] and '[TOC]' prepended" when: "the document is rendered" then: "the headings have ids 'привет' and 'привет_1', and the TOC contains 'Привет' and 'Привет'" - id: "AC-FR-001-03" scenario: "Heading with no word characters in any script still uses the existing fallback" given: "markdown.markdown('# !!!', extensions=['toc'])" when: "the document is rendered" then: "output is exactly '

!!!

' (unchanged behaviour)" - id: "AC-FR-001-04" scenario: "Existing ASCII and transliterable Latin slugs are unchanged" given: "markdown.markdown('# Header\\n\\n# žlutý kůň\\n\\n# Глава 1', extensions=['toc'])" when: "the document is rendered" then: "ids are exactly 'header', 'zluty-kun' and '1' respectively (unchanged behaviour)" - id: "AC-FR-001-05" scenario: "Custom slugify callable is not overridden" given: "TocExtension(slugify=lambda value, sep: '') and source '# Привет'" when: "the document is rendered" then: "the heading id is '_1' (the user's callable result is used as-is, as today)" - id: "AC-FR-001-06" scenario: "Custom separator is honoured in the fallback" given: "TocExtension(separator='_') and source '# Привет мир'" when: "the document is rendered" then: "the heading id is 'привет_мир'" - id: "AC-FR-001-07" scenario: "Behaviour is documented" given: "docs/extensions/toc.md, 'slugify' option entry" when: "inspected" then: "it states that, with the default slugify, headings whose ASCII slug would be empty receive a Unicode slug, and that slugify_unicode keeps non-ASCII characters for all headings" verification_method: "TEST" ``` ```yaml id: "FR-002" title: "Preserve combining marks in Unicode slugs" statement: "When producing a Unicode-preserving slug (slugify with unicode=True, slugify_unicode, and the FR-001 fallback), the system SHALL keep characters of Unicode categories Mn (non-spacing mark) and Mc (spacing combining mark) instead of removing them." epistemic_status: "INFERRED" source: "Issue #5: 'We write our docs in Hindi'; markdown/extensions/toc.py:45 (re.sub(r'[^\\w\\s-]', '', value) drops Mn/Mc characters because Python's \\w does not match them)" actor: "Documentation author writing headings in Devanagari or another script that uses combining marks" priority: "SHOULD_HAVE" readiness_status: "PROVISIONAL" dependencies: ["ASSUMP-003", "Q-003"] inputs: - {name: "value", type: "str", description: "Heading text passed to the slugify callable"} - {name: "separator", type: "str", description: "Word separator"} outputs: - {name: "slug", type: "str", description: "Unicode slug"} acceptance_criteria: - id: "AC-FR-002-01" scenario: "Hindi heading with slugify_unicode keeps vowel signs and virama" given: "from markdown.extensions.toc import slugify_unicode" when: "slugify_unicode('नमस्ते दुनिया', '-') is called" then: "the result is exactly 'नमस्ते-दुनिया' (today it is 'नमसत-दनय')" - id: "AC-FR-002-02" scenario: "Hindi heading with default toc configuration (combined with FR-001)" given: "markdown.markdown('# नमस्ते दुनिया', extensions=['toc'])" when: "the document is rendered" then: "output is exactly '

नमस्ते दुनिया

'" - id: "AC-FR-002-03" scenario: "Punctuation is still stripped in the Unicode path" given: "from markdown.extensions.toc import slugify_unicode" when: "slugify_unicode('Привет, мир!', '-') is called" then: "the result is exactly 'привет-мир'" - id: "AC-FR-002-04" scenario: "Existing Unicode behaviour without combining marks is unchanged" given: "TocExtension(permalink=True, slugify=slugify_unicode) and source '# Unicode ヘッダー'" when: "the document is rendered" then: "the heading id is 'unicode-ヘッダー' (existing test tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py:1199-1206 still passes)" - id: "AC-FR-002-05" scenario: "ASCII default path is unaffected" given: "from markdown.extensions.toc import slugify" when: "slugify('žlutý kůň', '-') is called" then: "the result is exactly 'zluty-kun'" verification_method: "TEST" ``` ## 3. Non-functional requirements None. ## 4. Assumptions and open questions **ASSUMP-001 [INFERRED]:** The improvement must not change any id that is non-empty under the current default `slugify`. Only ids that are `_n` today because their slug was empty may change. - *Rationale:* Python-Markdown is a widely used library. Changing default anchors would break existing permalinks for every Latin-script site. - *Impact if invalid:* MEDIUM. If maintainers want Unicode by default for all headings, FR-001 becomes "switch the default to `slugify_unicode`". - *Validation path:* Maintainer review of Q-002. **ASSUMP-002 [INFERRED]:** Ids that are `_1`, `_2`, … today (the ones that change under FR-001) carry no meaningful stability guarantee. - *Rationale:* The issue describes them as useless for sharing. - *Impact if invalid:* MEDIUM. If they must stay stable, the fallback has to become opt-in through a new config option. - *Validation path:* Q-001. Mention the change in the release notes. **ASSUMP-003 [INFERRED]:** Keeping Mn/Mc characters in Unicode slugs is acceptable even though it changes `slugify_unicode` output for input that contains combining marks. - *Rationale:* Removing them mangles words, which defeats the purpose of a Unicode slug. HTML5 `id` values may contain any non-whitespace characters. - *Impact if invalid:* LOW. FR-002 would be dropped, and Hindi slugs would stay mangled but non-empty. - *Validation path:* Q-003. **Q-001: How should the improvement be delivered?** - Options: - (a) Automatic fallback to a Unicode slug only when the ASCII slug is empty. Non-breaking for readable ids. - (b) Documentation only: point users to `slugify_unicode`. No behaviour change, but the issue stays unresolved for users who use the defaults. - (c) Add a new opt-in config flag.
